description: We are a team of students passionate about AI, software development, and agriculture. We want to explore how NASA data can help farmers make better decisions and adapt to changing field conditions. We are interested in building a practical, data-driven solution and learning together throughout the challenge. We welcome teammates with skills in agriculture, data science, design, and storytelling.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data", FieldWise brings environmental and agricultural information together to help assess field conditions and explore alternative crop rotation options.

The platform focuses on factors such as soil moisture, rainfall, temperature, vegetation health, and water stress. It uses transparent, rule-based analysis rather than AI or machine learning, allowing users to understand how available data influences the assessment.

details:
FieldWise – Smarter Farming Through Earth Observation

FieldWise is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make more informed crop rotation decisions and improve long-term soil health.

The platform brings together NASA Earth observation data, local environmental information, soil characteristics, crop requirements, and farmers' priorities to help evaluate agricultural conditions and explore suitable crop rotation alternatives.

Users can create a farm profile by providing its location, soil characteristics, irrigation information, current crops, and farming priorities. FieldWise then organizes the available environmental and agricultural information and applies transparent, rule-based analysis to examine crop suitability and potential rotation options.

The platform considers important agricultural factors such as soil properties, rainfall, temperature, wind, water availability, and other relevant environmental conditions. It also identifies missing or unavailable information instead of inventing values or treating missing data as zero. This helps users understand both the available evidence and the limitations of each analysis.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FieldWise aims to support more informed agricultural decisions, encourage sustainable crop rotation practices, promote better soil management, and help farmers understand how environmental conditions influence their agricultural choices. By combining Earth observation data with local agricultural knowledge, the platform seeks to make scientific information more accessible and useful for practical farming decisions.

Technology and Tools

FieldWise was developed as a web application using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Supabase for authentication and database management. The project integrates NASA Earth observation resources alongside local agricultural and environmental information. The analysis engine uses documented agricultural rules and crop characteristics rather than artificial intelligence or machine learning.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of FieldWise is its approach to connecting satellite-based environmental observations with practical farm-level decision-making. Instead of presenting raw environmental data alone, it organizes relevant information into an understandable farm analysis and compares possible crop rotation alternatives.

The platform also emphasizes transparency: it distinguishes available information from missing data, explains the basis of its recommendations, and avoids unsupported yield predictions, artificial scores, or misleading certainty.

Factors Considered

Our team considered soil health, climate conditions, rainfall, wind, water availability, crop characteristics, local agricultural conditions, farmers' priorities, data reliability, and the limitations of available environmental datasets.

FieldWise aims to bridge the gap between Earth observation science and everyday agricultural decisions, helping farmers explore more sustainable ways to manage their land.
